A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoT study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched despite content relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4 accuracy comparisons, component ablations, inference timing and human evaluation scores.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, timing, ablation and human evaluation results, together with illustrative outputs in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The PGRR candidate generation, preference evaluation and ranking, CPM aggregation, and final inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and the appendix prompts retain the same content.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same eight tasks and data sources. The descriptions move from v2 Appendix A.1 into v3 Section 4.1; the newly disclosed Game of 24 sample count does not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 3 retain CoT, Meta-prompting, ToT, GoT and BoT as comparators. Newly cited methods appear in related work or future-work discussion, without additional evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The models, one-shot/two-shot settings, warm-up choices, judge and metrics are retained. v3 supplies additional settings and calibration guidance for existing evaluations, without establishing a revised setting or a new evaluation.

E4.justification: The PGRR, Logic and CPM ablations, knowledge-boundary analysis, warm-up observations, and Game of 24/MGSM cases in Appendix B are retained. New case-study captions add no analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The three annotators were already documented in v2; v3's calibration guidance introduces no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1, both tables labeled Table 2, Figure 3 and Appendix B retain identical results. Human consistency scores remain 4.01 for one-shot and 4.32 for two-shot; no additional numerical or qualitative outcome is reported.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), including preference transitivity, ranking, knowledge-boundary thresholding and the timing expression, are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about preference-guided reverse reasoning, cognitive preference management, reasoning accuracy and efficiency, and known/unknown tasks.

C2.justification: The Limitations section adds automatic demonstration selection as future work and acknowledges model instability, suggesting hybrid candidate scoring as a possible mitigation. Existing result interpretations and the one-shot limitation on multi-source tasks remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 1,000 Game of 24 samples mixed from the two cited datasets, temperatures of 0.7 for candidate generation and 0.1 for reasoning instantiation, and timing through evaluation completion. Appendix C adds planned annotator calibration using pre-scored examples. These are disclosures, not established experimental changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds CoT-Kinetics and references supporting automatic demonstration selection and candidate reliability, while removing the Logic-of-Thought citation. The overall research positioning remains stable; BoT's publication update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: Dataset descriptions move from Appendix A.1 into Section 4.1, and knowledge-boundary evaluation prose moves from Section 4.4 to 4.3. There are limited explanatory additions, appendix renumbering and author-contact edits; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 and the knowledge-boundary table are relocated. v3 expands Figure 3's timing caption and adds Figure 6–9 captions to existing Appendix B boxes. The diagrams and performance plot themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves reproducibility and clarity through the newly reported sample count, sampling temperatures, timing scope and annotator-calibration guidance. Moving dataset details into the main text and captioning existing cases also improves navigation. These are useful refinements, while the method, empirical evidence and main claims remain unchanged.
